findings.item: C04-M01/M04 validation case '828 Cambie against cone A (near edge)', the 'Plan-edge misses' metric and the r1 change-log line
findings.issue: The tested point is the address point (geo_point_2d), not the site. I fetched the parcel for 828 Cambie St (site_id 031375499; vertices -123.11530,49.27785 / -123.11453,49.27735 / -123.11425,49.27753 / -123.11503,49.27803) and projected it to the EPSG:3157 grid. Two vertices lie about 39-40 m inside the cone A east edge and two lie about 39-40 m outside. The parcel therefore overlaps cone A by about 40 m. This fits the booklet summary, which places vertex F (105.71 m) under cone A. 'State: near edge' and '828 Cambie lies 0.19 m outside cone A' are false for the site, and a designer reading them would be misled.
findings.fix: Rename the case 'P828 address-point frame fixture'. It still tests 0.191 m outside in the grid, 0.192 m geodesic, and 2.78 m inside under mixed frames. Add a parcel fixture: the 828 Cambie parcel against cone A gives an inside-plan overlap of about 40 m, and with the T1a 105.71 m limit (unverified) the state comes from height. Delete the r1 change-log claim. The Site port must test parcel or footprint polygons, never address points.

findings.issue: L_gov is the cone with the smallest L + U95, and the HeadroomMap shows L_gov minus grade. Take cone X with L 120 m and U95 0.01 m (T1a), and cone Y with L 118 m and U95 6 m (T1b). X governs, so the map shows 120 m. A 119 m design is clear for X but within uncertainty for Y. The drag-to-try map therefore shows a clear headroom where the per-cone card warns. This breaks the spec's own zero-silent-clears metric.
findings.fix: The HeadroomMap should show two surfaces. Clear-below is min_i(L_i - U95_i) minus grade. Surely-above is min_i(L_i + U95_i) minus grade. Hatch the band between them as 'within uncertainty'. Per-cone states stay authoritative. Add the X/Y example as a state fixture.

findings.item: C04 13 Nov MVP cut list against MVP effort (11.5 person-days)
findings.issue: The cut list includes 'LiDAR origin z and grade', 17 origin windows, a 5 m downtown grade field and hypothetical-site mode. M07 (heightfield pipeline) and M06 (import and placement) have no MVP share. LAS tiles run from 16.45 MB to 2.74 GB, the downtown tile sizes are unknown (HEAD returns 403), and no gridding tool (laspy or PDAL on Windows) is named. The `python` on this machine reports 3.9, while the brief says 3.13. The 11.5 figure understates the MVP.
findings.fix: Add an M07 MVP share (about 2 person-days: download 11 origin tiles plus the T1b reference-roof tiles, grid the bare-earth class, write int16) and an M06 MVP share (about 1 person-day: place a block, base z from LiDAR). Name the tool and Python version. Alternatively, cut the 5 m grade field and precompute only the origin z values and reference-roof z values. Restate the total at about 14-15 person-days against the 'bad' threshold of 16.

findings.issue: At 13 Nov, only cones A, E and 22 (T1b, if their LiDAR roofs are measured) and 3.2.1 (T1a 123.201 m, unverified search summary) can carry a limit L. The other 20 of 24 cones, including the downtown 3.2.x and 9.x cones that matter most to entrants, will read 'limit unknown'. The spec never states this expected coverage, so the team may present the MVP as a height checker.
findings.fix: Print the coverage (for example 'limits estimated for 4 of 24 cones') on the node and in the PDF. Today, email views@vancouver.ca, the address the view-cones dataset metadata gives for site implications, asking for L and the origin elevation for each downtown cone. Prioritise T1b for the cones that cross downtown.

findings.item: HRDEM North Shore coverage (M07 and dataset entry)
findings.issue: 'Covers the North Shore peaks' is inferred from the item bbox (lat 49.00-49.51). LiDAR project footprints are irregular, and restricted watershed terrain may have no data. Coverage at the peaks is unverified.
findings.fix: Sample the DTM COG at the five peak coordinates and record any nodata. Fall back to CanElevation MRDEM (30 m, seamless) before SRTM, and record its CGVD2013 datum.

findings.issue: Averaging to 25-50 m cells lowers sharp summits. The Lions are rock pinnacles and are the named subject of several views. A 20-50 m loss at 24 km is 0.05-0.1 deg, the same size as the 0.02 deg render/profile test.
findings.fix: Use max-preserving downsampling, or keep 5 m tiles inside each cone's subject sector. Add a test: modelled summit z within 2 m of the source DTM maximum for the five peaks.

findings.issue: A fixed 20 x 15 km North Shore window is not derived from the cone sectors. Subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km from the origins, and the horizon ridge can lie beyond them.
findings.fix: Compute the extent as the union of each cone sector plus 2 deg, out to the first horizon-defining ridge (marched on MRDEM). Record it in the tile manifest.

findings.issue: The method says '1 m within 100 m of each origin', which is a 200 m square, 40,000 cells and 1.36 MB for 17 windows. The parameter uses a 100 m square and 0.34 MB.
findings.fix: Choose one radius, then restate the cells and bytes.

findings.item: Horizontal datum handling (M01 frame rule, proj4js definition)
findings.issue: '+proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80' with no datum shift implicitly treats the portal's 'WGS84' lon/lat as NAD83(CSRS). That is probably right for City layers, but the spec never says so. OSM footprints and GNSS points are in an ITRF-based WGS84 and can sit about 1-2 m off.
findings.fix: State the policy: City layers get no datum shift; OSM and GNSS inputs are flagged as a different frame and carry sigma_hdatum. Verify by overlaying LiDAR-2022 building-class points on parcel and footprint edges, and record the residual.

findings.item: Vista context heights (dataset entry for the Vista pack)
findings.issue: unified_manifest.json shows the supplied buildings were re-grounded on SRTM with z shifts of -12.24 to +21.61 m (median 0.48 m). Vista roof z therefore mixes SRTM error with OSM heights. The spec says only 'heights unverified'.
findings.fix: Record the shift range. Exclude Vista roof z from any parity test of absolute elevation; use the pack only for footprint and visual parity.

findings.issue: 982 B per building is unified_buildings.bin (9,722,568 B) divided by the 9,897 supplied buildings only. The 51,510 extension buildings use about 320 B each. Across all buildings, bins plus indexes give about 515 B.
findings.fix: Restate as '982 B (supplied mesh) / 320 B (extension) / 515 B (overall incl. index)' against the 50-60 B LOD1 target.

findings.issue: A lint that bans 'approved' and 'safe' in UI strings will hit legitimate data: the Table 1 'Date approved' column and 'Council-approved' citations.
findings.fix: Scope the lint to generated warning and card copy. Allow-list quoted source text and citation fields.

findings.issue: The model page (re-read) also lists cached input at $1, Batch and Flex at 50% of Standard, and Fast mode at 2x. It names no restricted release. The 'rejects some security prompts' line traces only to the community post's trusted-access cyber rollout.
findings.fix: Use Batch for bulk extraction and checks. Attribute the restriction note to S27, not S28.

sources_checked.note: Verified: observer far 45,000 m and fogFar 9,000 m (line 410); backdrop fog 42,000 m (line 433); fog cap 0.55; the hfov and pitch rule (report.js about lines 109-110); 161 function declarations; fixtures F1-F3; 38,684,239 B generated (38,656,461 B excluding labels and manifests); 9,897 plus 51,510 buildings; no LICENSE in any repo; 14 of 24 views at the 24 deg floor; 17 distinct origins. Recomputed QE-Barclay, cone A, ENU and drop figures, and the 2004 sheet rows.

verdict: Round 3 fixes every BLOCKER and MAJOR item from the previous critique except delivery scope, which is only partly fixed. The geodesy reproduces exactly. The frame rule, the seven states, U95, the release gate and the hypothetical-site mode are sound. Four problems remain. The 828 Cambie 'near edge' case tests an address point, but the parcel overlaps cone A by about 40 m. The HeadroomMap's L + U95 governing rule can show clears that the per-cone card contradicts. The MVP budget leaves out LiDAR gridding and block placement. Two 'unread' claims are false: the team already holds the 2026 Guidelines (accessed 2026-09-22) and the Brief. The team can start building now if the named conditions are met before the MVP release.
